hero.headline: NASA launches rescue mission to save falling Swift Observatory
hero.body:
NASA launched an emergency mission to prevent the Swift Observatory from crashing back to Earth. The 3,200-pound space telescope, which has been studying cosmic phenomena since its launch, began falling toward the planet due to increased atmospheric drag caused by recent solar storms. A robotic spacecraft lifted off aboard a Pegasus rocket to attempt a reboost operation that will raise the observatory's orbit and extend its operational life.

The Swift Observatory has operated for years detecting gamma-ray bursts and other transient astronomical events. Solar activity during recent years increased the density of Earth's upper atmosphere, creating more drag on satellites in low Earth orbit. This drag gradually pulled Swift lower, threatening to end its mission prematurely through an uncontrolled reentry. The telescope weighs more than 1.5 tons and contains sensitive scientific instruments that NASA hoped to keep operational.

The rescue mission launched using a Pegasus rocket, which is carried aloft by an aircraft before igniting and climbing to orbit. The robotic spacecraft will rendezvous with Swift and use its propulsion system to push the observatory into a higher, more stable orbit. This type of orbital rescue represents a new approach for NASA, which has not previously attempted such a mission to save an aging space telescope from atmospheric decay.

Solar storms pose increasing risks to satellites as the sun enters more active phases of its 11-year cycle. The storms send charged particles and radiation toward Earth, heating and expanding the upper atmosphere. This expansion creates additional resistance for spacecraft in low orbits, accelerating their decay. Hundreds of satellites operate in similar orbital ranges and face comparable risks during periods of high solar activity.

If successful, the reboost will buy Swift additional years of operation and demonstrate techniques that could be used to extend the lives of other at-risk spacecraft. The mission carries significance beyond saving a single telescope, as orbital debris and satellite longevity have become pressing issues for space agencies worldwide. NASA has not disclosed how much additional operational time the reboost might provide, but the emergency nature of the launch underscores the urgency of preventing an uncontrolled reentry of the massive observatory.

cards.headline: Millions gather in Tehran for funeral of slain Iranian leader Khamenei
cards.body:
Thousands of mourners converged on Tehran's Grand Mosalla mosque as Iran began a week of funeral ceremonies for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, the former supreme leader who was killed in February during U.S.-Israeli airstrikes. By early morning, crowds had waited through the night to enter the sprawling mosque, with many traveling for hours to pay their respects.

Khamenei, 86, led Iran for more than three decades before his assassination. The funeral also honored other family members killed in the same raid, including his 14-month-old granddaughter. By 8 a.m., the open-air mosque held approximately 10,000 people, separated into equal sections for men and women. The crowds chanted "Death to America" and "Death to Israel" as they mourned the slain leader.

The scale of the multi-day funeral reflects Iran's efforts to convey messages of resistance and national loss. Authorities expect up to 30 million people may attend events across six days and five cities. At the request of Iraqi politicians, Khamenei's body will also be carried through the Iraqi Shia cities of Karbala and Najaf.

The ceremonies featured religious songs, the national anthem, and eulogies traditionally reserved for martyrs. Men wept openly and beat their chests in anguish during the emotional proceedings. Revolutionary and religious music blared from competing sound systems before dawn. Throughout the grounds, yellow Hezbollah flags and Iranian flags were visible among the mourners. Hundreds of free food stations offered water, lemonade, kebabs, soup, and other refreshments to sustain those attending in the intense heat, which reached 36 degrees Celsius by midday.

One mourner, Fatima Khavari, expressed her grief, saying: "I felt like I had been crushed on the head when our leader was killed. He is the only true guide we have known."

However, the massive funeral did not represent all Iranians. While women attending the mosque wore traditional chadars, many women elsewhere in Tehran did not wear headscarves. Some Iranians chose not to attend the ceremonies, with traffic leaving the capital remaining busy despite government calls for participation.

A notable absence marked the proceedings: Mojtaba Khamenei, Ali Khamenei's designated successor, did not appear at the funeral on the second day of mourning. Three of Khamenei's other sons attended the funeral prayers, but the absence of his chosen heir drew significant attention. Iranian officials have not explained why Mojtaba Khamenei has not made a public appearance at the major national event.

The funeral comes more than four months after Khamenei's death in what sources describe as coordinated attacks marking a significant escalation in hostilities between Iran and the West. The ceremony demonstrated the scale of public mourning while also reflecting anger over his death, with crowds expressing demands for retaliation.

cards.headline: China expands coast guard patrols to waters east of Taiwan
cards.teaser: Beijing sent two ships to patrol eastern waters around Taiwan in a new campaign challenging the island's control of strategically important areas.
cards.body:
China has raised pressure on Taiwan by expanding coast guard patrols to include waters east of the island. Beijing deployed two ships to patrol the area in what represents a new phase of its campaign to challenge Taiwan's authority over surrounding waters.

The waters east of Taiwan hold strategic importance for any potential future invasion scenario. By extending patrols to this region, China is demonstrating its capacity to operate in areas previously considered under Taiwan's effective control, marking an escalation in Beijing's military pressure campaign against the island.

cards.headline: Trump to attend NATO summit in Turkey as questions swirl over alliance unity
cards.teaser: President Trump heads to Turkey for a NATO summit where alliance cohesion faces pressure amid demands for increased burden-sharing.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump is set to attend a NATO summit in Turkey that will test unity among alliance members. The gathering comes as Trump has called for greater contributions from member nations and what some describe as demands for loyalty beyond traditional burden-sharing agreements.

Turkey's status within NATO has risen in recent years, bolstered by its weapons manufacturing capabilities and its relationship with the Trump administration. The summit location in Turkey reflects the country's growing influence within the alliance, with President Erdogan's warm ties to Trump offering Ankara additional leverage heading into the meetings.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Proposes 702 Regulatory Rollbacks
cards.body:
The Trump administration has outlined plans to eliminate or modify 702 federal regulations as part of an expanded deregulatory effort. The proposed changes span multiple agencies and sectors, representing one of the largest regulatory reduction initiatives in recent US history.

The semiannual regulatory agenda includes proposed rollbacks across the Treasury Department, Internal Revenue Service, and other federal agencies. The administration's deregulatory actions now stand at a ratio of 129 regulatory eliminations or modifications for every one new regulation introduced. White House officials have characterized the initiative as removing barriers to economic growth and reducing compliance costs for businesses.

The 702 proposed cuts include changes to financial regulations, tax compliance requirements, and industry oversight rules. The Treasury Department and Internal Revenue Service regulatory agenda accounts for a significant portion of the planned rollbacks. The administration has framed the effort as fulfilling campaign promises to reduce the size and scope of federal regulation.

Business groups have generally welcomed the regulatory reduction plans, while consumer advocates and regulatory experts have raised concerns about potential gaps in oversight and enforcement. The proposed changes will undergo varying review processes depending on their scope and legal requirements. Some modifications can be implemented through executive action, while others may require formal rulemaking procedures that include public comment periods.

The announcement marks a continuation of deregulatory policies that began during the administration's first term. The scale of the current proposal significantly exceeds previous efforts and signals an acceleration of regulatory rollbacks across the federal government. Implementation timelines for the 702 proposed changes vary, with some already in progress and others still in preliminary stages of review.

According to reports, the deregulatory push represents a major policy priority for the administration as it enters a new phase of governance. The breadth of the proposed rollbacks demonstrates a comprehensive approach to reducing federal oversight across multiple sectors of the economy.

The administration has made aggressive deregulation a central focus of its agenda, with these 702 proposed changes representing the latest step in that direction. As the various regulatory agencies process these proposals, the ultimate impact on different industries and consumer protections will become clearer. The coming months will reveal which proposed rollbacks move forward through the required approval processes and which face legal or procedural obstacles.

The scale and speed of the deregulatory effort underscore the administration's commitment to reshaping the federal regulatory landscape, though the full consequences of these changes remain to be seen as implementation proceeds across multiple agencies and sectors.

cards.headline: Three Small Nuclear Reactors Reach Operating Status in US
cards.teaser: The United States now has three advanced microreactors running, meeting an administration deadline and drawing attention from data center operators.
cards.body:
Three small-scale nuclear reactors have achieved criticality and begun operations, marking a milestone for advanced nuclear technology development in the United States. The Energy Secretary confirmed the third reactor reached operational status, meeting a deadline set by the administration for new nuclear capacity deployment.

The microreactors represent emerging nuclear technology designed for smaller-scale power generation compared to traditional reactors. Technology companies operating energy-intensive data centers have expressed interest in the reactors as potential power sources. The successful operation of multiple units provides real-world performance data for the developing advanced reactor industry, though significant regulatory and scaling challenges remain before widespread commercial deployment.

cards.headline: Far-left primary victories pose challenge for House Democratic leadership
cards.teaser: A growing wave of primary wins by democratic socialists could complicate House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries' path if Democrats retake the House in midterms.
cards.body:
The increasing number of primary victories by democratic socialists is poised to create a challenge for House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries if Democrats retake the House in the midterm elections. The New York Democrat will likely need to manage an increasingly active left flank as he pursues the Speakership.

The trend reflects a shift within the Democratic caucus as progressive candidates continue to win competitive primary races. Jeffries would need to balance the demands of the party's left wing with moderate members and his own leadership agenda if Democrats gain the majority.

cards.headline: Super typhoon Bavi triggers evacuations in Guam ahead of Monday landfall
cards.teaser: The storm is forecast to bring winds exceeding 160 mph and waves nearly 11 meters high when it makes landfall.
cards.body:
Authorities in Guam have ordered evacuations as super typhoon Bavi bears down on the island. The storm is expected to make landfall on Monday, bringing destructive conditions across the territory.

Forecasters predict extreme winds exceeding 160 mph and waves reaching nearly 11 meters in height. These powerful conditions pose major threats to coastal infrastructure and communities throughout Guam.

cards.headline: Trump to attend NATO summit in Turkey as questions swirl over alliance unity
cards.teaser: President Trump heads to Turkey for a NATO summit where alliance cohesion faces pressure amid demands for increased burden-sharing.

cards.headline: China releases detained pastor after Trump raises case with Xi Jinping
cards.teaser: Ezra Jin Mingri, founder of an underground church, was freed nearly two months after President Trump discussed his detention with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
cards.body:
Pastor Ezra Jin Mingri, who leads the prominent underground Zion Church, has been released from Chinese detention. Jin was imprisoned as part of Beijing's broader crackdown on religious activities operating outside state control.

The pastor's release came nearly two months after President Trump raised his case directly with Chinese President Xi Jinping during a visit to Beijing. Trump's intervention appears to have influenced the Chinese government's decision to free him.

cards.headline: Ukrainian forces deny Russian claims of eastern city capture
cards.teaser: Ukraine's military says its troops are holding out against infiltrating Russian forces in the Donetsk region despite Kremlin claims.
cards.body:
Ukraine's military has rejected Russian claims that Moscow's forces have captured a city in the eastern Donetsk region. Ukrainian commanders say their troops continue to defend positions against Russian soldiers attempting to infiltrate the area.

The fighting continues amid the grinding conflict on the eastern front, where soldiers navigate ruined structures and evade drone surveillance. The disputed city lies far from both Kyiv and Moscow, representing one of many contested positions along the extensive front line where both sides claim territorial gains.

cards.headline: Venezuela's public housing vulnerabilities exposed after earthquakes
cards.teaser: Residents, construction experts, and seismologists had warned for years that Venezuela's public housing would be at risk in a natural disaster.
cards.body:
Years of warnings about the structural integrity of Venezuela's public housing preceded recent earthquakes that struck the country. Residents, construction experts, and seismologists had repeatedly raised concerns that the buildings would prove vulnerable during a natural disaster.

The earthquakes that hit Venezuela's northern coast exposed these risks, with widespread damage across the region. Residencia La Gabarra, a 12-storey beachside apartment block in La Guaira, collapsed into rubble, trapping residents including at least three children. The disaster prompted thousands of volunteers and international rescue teams to search for survivors in the aftermath.

hero.headline: Trump delivers address marking America's 250th birthday
hero.teaser: President Donald Trump spoke at July 4th celebrations honoring war veterans and American history while including elements of his political agenda.
hero.body:
President Donald Trump delivered a late-night speech in Washington DC on Saturday to commemorate the United States' 250th anniversary. The address, which began at 11:15 p.m., incorporated Trump's political messaging alongside recognition of American history and military service members.

Trump characterized the country as "a nation of winners" and stated that "today our country is winning again." He claimed the US was "just getting started" and vowed to take the nation "to new levels," invoking the concept of a "golden age of America." The president highlighted what he described as the country's "unmatched achievement and unlimited potential."

The celebrations were significantly disrupted by severe weather. An extreme heatwave swept across the US East Coast, with temperatures exceeding 100 degrees Fahrenheit in Washington. By 8 p.m. on Saturday, emergency services had treated 51 people for heat-related issues, with 12 requiring hospitalization. A passing thunderstorm forced evacuators to clear the event site for more than two hours due to lightning and rain concerns. Despite the evacuation, crowds returned to witness the speech and subsequent fireworks display.

The festivities featured what organizers billed as the largest fireworks display in world history. Trump introduced military veterans and the crew of the Artemis II lunar mission while discussing moments from American history. He described the country as "the hope, the promise, the light and the glory" of the world.

Throughout the weekend's celebrations, Trump delivered multiple addresses with partisan political content. On Friday evening at Mount Rushmore in South Dakota, he launched an attack on what he termed the "communist menace" in America, characterizing communism supporters as enemies of American independence. He reiterated these themes during his Washington speech, stating that communism "never worked, and it never will work."

The celebrations were marred by additional complications. The National Mall's reflecting pool, which Trump had ordered renovated for $14.7 million to turn "American Flag blue," remained green due to an algae bloom. Trump and his officials blamed vandals for the project's failure. The Independence Day parade in Washington was canceled due to extreme heat, as was a parade in Philadelphia, where the Declaration of Independence was signed in 1776.

Trump's allies have faced accusations of using the anniversary celebrations to intensify rather than bridge the country's divisions, transforming a traditionally nonpartisan patriotic moment into a vehicle for political messaging. His living predecessors were notably absent from the main events in Washington.

Despite the weather challenges, Trump pointed to the crowd's return after evacuation as an example of American resilience. "You heard it was over," he told attendees. "And what happened? You came back."

cards.headline: Severe weather disrupts July 4th celebrations across the U.S.
cards.teaser: Storms and extreme heat forced evacuations and cancellations at Independence Day events nationwide during the 250th birthday celebrations.
cards.body:
Extreme heat and severe storms threatened America's 250th birthday celebrations nationwide. The National Mall was evacuated due to weather conditions, and multiple July 4th events across Pennsylvania and New Jersey were canceled as dangerous conditions persisted throughout the day.

Philadelphia's Unity Concert for America and fireworks display experienced significant delays but ultimately proceeded. The event featured performances from The Roots, Meek Mill, and Will Smith, who closed out the program for attendees who waited out the weather disruptions.

cards.headline: Paul Pelosi involved in California hit-and-run, authorities say
cards.teaser: The husband of former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi was involved in a hit-and-run incident that left a parked car with major damage.
cards.body:
Paul Pelosi, husband of former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, was involved in a hit-and-run incident in California on Saturday. The collision damaged a parked car, leaving it with significant harm.

Authorities announced the incident on Saturday but provided limited additional details about what occurred.

cards.headline: Eight people shot in Coney Island, four children among those injured
cards.teaser: At least eight people were shot in Coney Island, New York, on Saturday evening, including four children, according to the New York Police Department.
cards.body:
At least eight people, including four children, were shot in Coney Island on July 4th during Independence Day celebrations. Police responded to reports of gunfire at approximately 10:37 p.m. on West 31st Street in the Brooklyn neighborhood. One woman was reported in critical condition.

The shooting occurred late in the evening as crowds gathered to observe the holiday festivities in the popular beachside area. The New York City Police Department is investigating the incident.

cards.headline: Pastor released from Chinese prison weeks after Trump raised case with Xi
cards.teaser: A pastor detained in China in October has been freed less than two months after President Trump discussed his case with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
cards.body:
Ezra Jin, founder of the prominent underground Zion Church, has been released from detention in China and reunited with his family in the United States. Jin landed in the US on Friday evening after being detained during a sweeping crackdown on Christians in October that affected dozens of church members.

The release comes weeks after President Donald Trump raised Jin's case during a meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, requesting his freedom from prison.

cards.headline: England to face Mexico at Azteca Stadium in World Cup last 16
cards.teaser: England prepares to play Mexico at the historic Azteca Stadium, one of the most significant venues in international football history.
cards.body:
England will face Mexico in the last 16 of the World Cup at the Azteca Stadium, returning to the venue for the first time in 40 years. The match is scheduled for a 1am kick-off time for viewers in England.

The Azteca Stadium holds iconic status in football history as one of the sport's great venues, where significant matches and championship moments have taken place throughout the years. Mexico is co-hosting the World Cup tournament.

cards.headline: Norway faces Brazil as Haaland feuds reach World Cup stage
cards.teaser: The Premier League tension between Manchester City's Erling Haaland and Arsenal takes on a global dimension as Norway meets Brazil.
cards.body:
Manchester City's Erling Haaland will face Brazil in World Cup competition as Norway takes on the South American team. The match brings Premier League tensions to the international stage, as Haaland has been involved in disputes with Arsenal during domestic competition.

The World Cup encounter represents the first time the Premier League feud between Haaland and Arsenal will play out on the global stage. Norway enters the match as the underdog against Brazil, one of football's traditional powers.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Drop as Supply Increases Revive Oversupply Concerns
cards.teaser: Global oil markets face renewed fears of oversupply as prices tumble for the fourth consecutive week.
cards.body:
Oil prices have fallen for the fourth straight week as increased supply flows and easing geopolitical tensions push markets toward potential oversupply conditions. Brent crude prices have returned to pre-conflict levels, with analysts at Citi forecasting the benchmark could drop to $60 per barrel by year end if current supply trends continue.

The Strait of Hormuz has seen normalized shipping flows following recent US-Iran diplomatic efforts, removing a key risk premium from oil markets. The combination of rising production and reduced geopolitical risk has shifted market sentiment from concerns about shortages to worries about excess supply heading into the second half of the year.

cards.headline: Bending Spoons Shares Jump 40% in Market Debut
cards.teaser: The Italian software company behind acquisitions of AOL, Vimeo, and other internet brands saw strong first-day trading after an $18 billion IPO.
cards.body:
Bending Spoons, an Italian technology company valued at $23 billion, saw its shares rise 40% in its stock market debut following an initial public offering. The company has built its business model around acquiring and revitalizing older internet brands including AOL and Vimeo.

The company's founder attributed its success to strategies designed to minimize reliance on luck in business outcomes. Bending Spoons has positioned itself to capitalize on opportunities created by artificial intelligence technology while managing a portfolio of established but struggling internet properties. The strong market reception reflects investor interest in the company's acquisition-focused growth strategy.

cards.headline: PECO Workers Begin First Strike in Company History
cards.teaser: Utility workers in Pennsylvania walked off the job during a heat wave after contract negotiations failed.
cards.body:
Members of IBEW Local 614 initiated the first strike in PECO's history after the utility company and union failed to reach agreement on a new contract. The work stoppage began during a heat wave affecting the Philadelphia region, raising concerns about service and repairs during peak demand.

The union reported three workers were injured on picket lines, allegations the company called false. The strike affects workers responsible for maintaining and repairing electrical infrastructure for customers across southeastern Pennsylvania. Contract disputes center on wages, benefits, and working conditions, though specific terms under negotiation have not been publicly detailed.

cards.headline: Electric Vehicle Batteries Show Greater Durability Than Projected
cards.teaser: Real-world data shows EV batteries lasting significantly longer than initial estimates suggested.
cards.body:
Electric vehicle batteries are demonstrating longer lifespans than manufacturers and researchers initially expected, according to data from vehicles with hundreds of thousands of miles of use. A Stanford study found EV batteries last approximately 40% longer in real-world conditions compared to earlier laboratory-based projections.

The findings address longstanding consumer concerns about battery replacement costs and vehicle longevity. Battery degradation has been slower than feared across multiple manufacturers and vehicle types. The improved durability data could influence used EV market values and total cost of ownership calculations that factor in potential battery replacement expenses.

cards.headline: Trump Accounts Launch for Children's Savings
cards.teaser: A new government-backed savings program for minors debuted on Independence Day with support from corporate donors.
cards.body:
Trump Accounts, a new savings program for children, launched on July 4th with government backing from congressional Republicans. All accounts opened for children born between January 2025 and December 2028 will receive $1,000 from the government. Parents, friends, and employers can contribute up to $5,000 annually to each account.

The accounts are investment vehicles managed by major Wall Street firms. Michael Dell, founder of Dell Technologies, made an initial contribution to support the program. The initiative aims to provide American families with accessible savings options for their children's financial futures.

cards.headline: Blue whales sing at frequencies killer whales cannot hear
cards.teaser: Research shows blue whale calls occur at such low frequencies that their only natural predator cannot detect them beyond one kilometer.
cards.body:
A University of Washington researcher published findings in 2025 showing that blue whales produce calls at frequencies so low that killer whales cannot hear them. Beyond one kilometer, these deep-frequency songs become completely undetectable to orca ears.

Blue whales use extremely low-frequency vocalizations to communicate across vast ocean distances. Since killer whales, their only natural predator, cannot perceive these deep frequencies, the whales effectively hide through acoustic stealth while coordinating and navigating in the surrounding waters.

cards.headline: Astronomers find massive paired structures that challenge cosmology
cards.teaser: Two enormous cosmic structures appear in the same region of space at the same distance, a configuration that current cosmological models struggle to explain.
cards.body:
Two colossal cosmic structures—the Giant Arc and the Big Ring—have been discovered in the same region of deep space at identical distances from Earth. Astronomer Alexia Lopez, who helped identify them, says their unexpected pairing challenges current cosmological models.

The discovery raises questions about the universe's large-scale structure. Scientists have long assumed matter distributes relatively uniformly when viewed at the largest scales, but these paired megastructures suggest the universe may contain organizational patterns that existing theories don't predict.

cards.headline: Fossils show dinosaurs thriving before asteroid impact
cards.teaser: New Mexico fossils reveal dinosaurs were flourishing in diverse ecosystems when the asteroid struck 66 million years ago, contradicting earlier theories of decline.
cards.body:
A 2025 study published in Science challenges the century-old assumption that dinosaurs were declining before the asteroid impact 66 million years ago. Fossils discovered in New Mexico reveal that dinosaurs were actually flourishing in diverse, thriving ecosystems at the time of the strike.

The fossil evidence shows healthy, varied dinosaur populations occupied different ecological niches right up until the impact. This finding suggests the asteroid delivered a sudden catastrophe to robust dinosaur communities rather than hastening the demise of already struggling species.

cards.headline: SpaceX launches Starlink satellites with semiconductor test bed
cards.teaser: A Falcon 9 rocket carried 24 Starlink satellites and a semiconductor manufacturing test bed into orbit from Florida.
cards.body:
SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 rocket carrying 24 Starlink satellites along with a semiconductor manufacturing test bed. The mission lifted off from Florida, adding to the growing constellation of internet satellites while also carrying an experiment designed to test chip fabrication processes in space. The dual-purpose launch demonstrates how commercial satellite operators can share launch capacity with research payloads.

The semiconductor test bed will evaluate manufacturing processes in the microgravity environment of orbit. Separate SpaceX launches also continued from California, with another Falcon 9 mission deploying additional Starlink satellites. The company maintains a rapid launch cadence, regularly sending batches of satellites into low Earth orbit to expand global internet coverage while occasionally accommodating experimental hardware from research institutions and commercial partners.

cards.headline: Voyager 1 continues sending data 22 light-hours from Earth
cards.teaser: The probe launched in 1977 remains operational in interstellar space, with radio signals now taking over 22 hours to reach it.
cards.body:
Voyager 1, launched in 1977, remains the most distant active human spacecraft. Radio signals now take over 22 hours to reach it traveling at light speed, yet it continues transmitting data from interstellar space using a power source comparable to a car battery. This remarkable longevity far exceeds its original four-year mission timeline.

The spacecraft's ability to operate in the extreme environment of deep space contrasts sharply with Earth-based technology. While data centres require 10 to 30 percent of their energy budget just for cooling using millions of litres of water, Voyager 1 relies on radiator panels to shed waste heat directly into space as infrared radiation—a far more efficient solution where no atmosphere or cooling infrastructure exists.

cards.headline: Orbital data centers could eliminate water cooling requirements
cards.teaser: Space-based data centers would use radiator panels to dissipate heat as infrared light instead of consuming millions of liters of water.
cards.body:
Cooling data centers on Earth consumes 10 to 30 percent of their energy budget and millions of liters of water annually. In space, the absence of air and traditional cooling infrastructure creates a fundamentally different thermal environment. Orbital data centers could instead use radiator panels to release waste heat as infrared light into the vacuum.

This approach would eliminate water consumption while addressing a major environmental and operational challenge for computing infrastructure. As demand for computing power increases, space-based cooling represents an alternative to conventional methods constrained by water availability and energy costs on Earth.

hero.headline: France advances to World Cup quarterfinals with penalty kick victory over Paraguay
hero.body:
France secured a quarterfinal berth at the 2026 World Cup with a hard-fought victory over Paraguay in Philadelphia. Kylian Mbappé converted a second-half penalty to break the deadlock against a Paraguay side that employed physical tactics throughout the match.

The goal was Mbappé's 19th in World Cup competition, moving him within one of Lionel Messi in the race for the Golden Boot at this tournament. France, considered among the favorites to win the World Cup, had previously dismantled opponents in earlier rounds but needed to find a different approach against Paraguay's defensive strategy.

Paraguay's tactics drew criticism from observers who described their approach as using dark arts to frustrate the French attack. The physical nature of the match forced France to adapt their style of play. Mbappé addressed the tactics after the match, stating that France could also get their hands dirty when necessary. The Paraguay coach made no complaints about the result despite his team's elimination.

The victory in Philadelphia continues France's pursuit of the World Cup title as they navigate the knockout stages. Their next opponent in the quarterfinals has not yet been determined. The match marked a test of France's ability to win in different ways beyond their attacking dominance shown in group play.

France's progression sets up a potential deep run in the tournament as they seek to claim the World Cup. The team has demonstrated both offensive firepower in earlier matches and the resilience to grind out results when facing determined defensive opposition. Paraguay exits the competition after pushing one of the tournament's strongest teams to find an alternative path to victory.

cards.headline: Sabalenka and Osaka to meet for third time in three months at Wimbledon
cards.teaser: Aryna Sabalenka and Naomi Osaka will face each other in the Wimbledon round of 16 for a spot in the quarterfinals.
cards.body:
Aryna Sabalenka and Naomi Osaka will face off at Wimbledon in the Round of 16, with a quarterfinal spot on the line. This marks their third meeting in just three months.

The two players have developed a rivalry through their frequent matchups leading up to this grass court Grand Slam clash.

cards.headline: Dodgers place four starters on All-Star Game roster led by Ohtani and Freeman
cards.teaser: The Los Angeles Dodgers matched for most All-Star selections with four players named starters including Shohei Ohtani and Freddie Freeman.
cards.body:
The Dodgers are sending four players to the MLB All-Star Game as starters, tying the Braves and Phillies for the most selections from any team. Shohei Ohtani and Freddie Freeman headline the Los Angeles representatives chosen to start the midsummer showcase.

The full All-Star rosters were unveiled with 26 first-time selections across both leagues.

cards.headline: Darryn Peterson scores 28 points in summer league debut for Jazz
cards.teaser: Rookie Darryn Peterson posted 28 points in his first NBA Summer League game as the Utah Jazz defeated the Atlanta Hawks in overtime.
cards.body:
Darryn Peterson made an immediate impact in his NBA Summer League debut for the Utah Jazz, scoring 28 points to help his team secure an overtime victory against the Atlanta Hawks. The performance lived up to expectations for the highly regarded rookie.

Peterson was among several top prospects who performed well in their summer league debuts. Cameron Boozer also had a strong showing in his first game. The Jazz earned the win in extra time behind Peterson's offensive output.

cards.headline: England prepares to face Mexico at Azteca Stadium in World Cup knockout round
cards.teaser: England will play Mexico at the historic Azteca Stadium in Mexico City in the round of 16 at the World Cup.
cards.body:
England will face Mexico in the World Cup last 16 at the Azteca Stadium in Mexico City, returning to the iconic venue for the first time in 40 years. The stadium holds significant historical importance in world football, having hosted many memorable matches throughout its storied past.

Head coach Thomas Tuchel has warned his team to remain focused as they prepare for the knockout clash. England's arrival in Mexico City has already drawn attention from local fans, with the team's hotel location becoming known to supporters ahead of the match.

cards.headline: Mexico returns luxury watches from YouTuber due to FIFA gift rules
cards.teaser: The Mexico national team returned luxury watches given to them by a content creator because FIFA regulations prohibit expensive gifts.
cards.body:
Mexico's World Cup squad returned luxury watches gifted by a content creator after determining the presents violated FIFA regulations. The governing body prohibits players from accepting expensive gifts during the tournament.

The decision ensures the team complies with tournament rules ahead of their match against England.

cards.headline: Premier League rivalry between Haaland and Arsenal set for World Cup stage
cards.teaser: The Premier League feud takes on global significance as Norway meets Brazil at the World Cup.
cards.body:
A Premier League rivalry is poised to reach the World Cup stage as Norway prepares to face Brazil in tournament play. The match will feature Manchester City striker Erling Haaland in a high-profile international fixture.

The encounter represents a shift from domestic competition to the global stage for the Norwegian forward. The match between Norway and Brazil brings Premier League storylines into World Cup knockout competition.

hero.headline: Sky buying ITV could reshape British television landscape
hero.body:
Sky is set to acquire ITV's television and streaming channels in a deal expected to be announced imminently, a move that could significantly reshape the British broadcasting industry. The acquisition would bring together two major players in UK media, combining Sky's satellite and streaming platform with ITV's free-to-air channels and content library.

The transaction involves ITV's broadcasting and streaming operations, which include multiple television channels and the ITVX streaming service. ITV operates several of Britain's most-watched channels, including ITV1, ITV2, and other themed networks that broadcast popular dramas, entertainment programs, and news content. The acquisition would give Sky control over a substantial portion of British television programming and distribution.

Viewers may see changes to how ITV programming is distributed and accessed following the deal. Sky currently operates its own subscription-based television service and the NOW streaming platform, while ITV has traditionally been available free-to-air to UK households. The integration of ITV's channels into Sky's portfolio could affect programming strategies, commissioning decisions, and how content is made available to audiences. Popular ITV shows spanning drama series, reality television, and daytime programming would fall under Sky's ownership.

The deal comes as traditional broadcasters face increasing competition from streaming services and changing viewing habits. Both Sky and ITV have been adapting their strategies to compete with platforms like Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+. Sky is owned by Comcast, the American media and telecommunications company, which acquired the broadcaster in 2018. ITV has been working to grow its streaming presence while maintaining its position as a major commercial broadcaster in the UK.

The acquisition will require regulatory approval from UK authorities who oversee media ownership and competition. Regulators will examine whether the combined entity would reduce competition in the broadcasting market and how it might affect content diversity and viewer choice. The announcement is expected to provide more details about the structure of the deal, its financial terms, and Sky's plans for integrating ITV's operations.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift marries Travis Kelce in secret wedding ceremony
cards.teaser: The singer and football player wed in a private ceremony that included celebrity guests and personal touches from Swift's music catalog.
cards.body:
Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce married in a secret wedding ceremony featuring comedian Adam Sandler among the guests and handkerchiefs printed with lyrics from Swift's song "Blank Space." Swift's aunt revealed that both the bride and groom cried during the ceremony. The couple wore outfits designed by a Northern Irish designer.

The wedding took place amid Swift's long history of Fourth of July celebrations, with activity observed at her Rhode Island estate as fireworks went off in the area. Swift has hosted star-studded Fourth of July parties at the property in previous years. The couple had kept their wedding plans private, with details emerging only after the ceremony took place.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift's former teacher dies of cancer on singer's wedding day
cards.teaser: A teacher described as one of Swift's biggest supporters and a former security guard died at age 69 after battling cancer.
cards.body:
A teacher who was reportedly one of Taylor Swift's favorites and described as one of her biggest supporters died after a battle with cancer on the same day the singer married Travis Kelce. The educator, who also worked as a security guard, was 69 years old.

The teacher had been identified as an important figure in Swift's life and educational background. The timing of the death coinciding with Swift's wedding day has been noted across multiple reports covering both events.

cards.headline: Jesse Eisenberg says leaving U.S. over Trump would be silly
cards.teaser: The actor and director said he feels a responsibility to stay in New York City despite recently obtaining Polish citizenship.
cards.body:
Actor and director Jesse Eisenberg said he has no plans to leave the United States, despite recently becoming a Polish citizen. Speaking at the Karlovy Vary Film Festival, where he received the President's Award, Eisenberg indicated he feels committed to staying in the country and rejected the idea of relocating over political concerns.

Eisenberg, who directed "A Real Pain," also discussed his new film "The Debut," which he characterized as the opposite of artificial intelligence. This comment came following A24's partnership with DeepMind.

cards.headline: Death Valley actor Gwyneth Keyworth says ADHD diagnosis helped her acting
cards.teaser: The actress said the condition made her feel lucky she found acting and helped her identify with her character.
cards.body:
Gwyneth Keyworth, who stars in "Death Valley," said her ADHD diagnosis made her feel fortunate to have found acting as a profession. The actress plays detective Janie Mallowan in the series.

Keyworth said the condition helped her identify with and connect to her character. She described the diagnosis as providing insight into how she approaches her work as an actor.

cards.headline: Manga series Murcilago to get anime adaptation in 2027
cards.teaser: The series by Yoshimura Kana, which has sold more than 2.3 million copies, will stream on HIDIVE in the U.S. and Canada.
cards.body:
"Murcilago," a manga by Yoshimura Kana, is being adapted into a television anime set to premiere in 2027. HIDIVE announced it will stream the series exclusively in the United States, Canada, and several other markets. The adaptation was revealed at Anime Expo 2026.

The manga has been serialized in Square Enix's Young Gangan magazine since August 2013 and has sold more than 2.3 million copies. HIDIVE secured streaming rights for multiple territories for the upcoming television adaptation.

cards.headline: Noah Wyle says he missed roles in major films while filming ER
cards.teaser: The actor said he was offered parts in Saving Private Ryan and Good Night, and Good Luck but could not get out of his commitment to the medical series.
cards.body:
Noah Wyle recently revealed that his commitment to "ER" cost him opportunities to appear in major films. While starring in the long-running medical drama, Wyle was offered roles in "Saving Private Ryan" and "Good Night, and Good Luck" but had to turn them down due to scheduling conflicts with the series.

Wyle discussed these missed opportunities during an appearance on the "Still Here Hollywood" podcast, noting that such conflicts occurred multiple times during his years on "ER."

hero.headline: Trump marks 250th anniversary with speech blending patriotism and partisan rhetoric
hero.body:
President Trump delivered a late-night speech on the National Mall to mark America's 250th anniversary, combining celebrations of American achievements with pointed partisan political messaging. The address began at 11:15 p.m. after being delayed by severe thunderstorms that forced spectators to evacuate for more than two hours before returning to the site.

The president hailed the "unmatched achievement and unlimited potential" of the United States, declaring the nation was "just getting started" and vowing to take it "to new levels." He framed the milestone as one of the most joyous occasions in history while repeatedly emphasizing what he characterized as ideological threats to the country.

A central theme of Trump's remarks focused on communism. He claimed that communism posed an existential threat to America, stating "we don't want communists in our country" and describing it as something that "never worked, and it never will work." This attack on what he termed the "communist menace" extended rhetoric from his earlier speech at Mount Rushmore in South Dakota on Friday, where he framed supporters of communism as "the enemy of July 4th 1776."

The president's speech departed sharply from the traditionally nonpartisan tone that American presidents have customarily adopted on Independence Day. Living predecessors notably absented themselves from the main Washington events. Trump highlighted military veterans and the Artemis II lunar mission crew while referencing select moments of American history. He also emphasized Christian values in his vision for the nation's future and promoted his legislative priorities.

Extreme weather significantly disrupted the 250th anniversary celebrations. A dangerous heatwave blanketed more than two dozen states, with temperatures exceeding 100 degrees Fahrenheit in Washington. Emergency services treated 51 people for heat-related issues, with 12 hospitalized. The sweltering conditions forced cancellations of Independence Day parades in both Washington and Philadelphia.

When thunderstorms approached the National Mall during the evening, spectators evacuated amid lightning and heavy rain. Trump responded to the disruption on social media, suggesting that "storms bring luck to whatever the occasion" and claiming he would have spoken even "in front of one person at four o'clock in the morning" if necessary.

The speech concluded just before midnight with what organizers billed as the largest fireworks display in world history. Trump had previously urged Americans to attend, promising "the greatest show of all" and claiming the fireworks would be "10 times larger" than any previously conducted on American soil.

The president used the weather disruption as an example of American resilience, telling the crowd that many people had returned after being sent away. Security around the National Mall was notably heightened, with thousands of National Guard troops stationed throughout Washington.

cards.headline: Treasury unveils new currency bearing Trump signature for 250th anniversary
cards.teaser: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent displayed new U.S. currency featuring President Trump's signature, set to enter circulation for the nation's 250th birthday.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled new U.S. currency featuring President Trump's signature ahead of the nation's 250th anniversary celebration. The redesigned $100 bill will carry both Bessent's and Trump's signatures and is scheduled to enter circulation soon as part of the semiquincentennial commemoration.

The announcement coincided with Trump's late-night speech in Washington DC marking the milestone anniversary, in which he emphasized America's achievements and potential. The new currency represents a visible change to American paper money as the country observes its 250th birthday throughout the year.

cards.headline: Far-left primary victories pose challenge for House Democratic leadership
cards.teaser: A growing wave of primary wins by democratic socialists could complicate House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries' path if Democrats retake the House in midterms.
cards.body:
The increasing number of primary victories by democratic socialists is poised to create a challenge for House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries if Democrats retake the House in the midterm elections. The New York Democrat will likely need to manage an increasingly active left flank as he pursues the Speakership.

The trend reflects a shift within the Democratic caucus as progressive candidates continue to win competitive primary races. Jeffries would need to balance the demands of the party's left wing with moderate members and his own leadership agenda if Democrats gain the majority.

cards.headline: White supremacist group marches through Washington during anniversary celebrations
cards.teaser: Masked members of white supremacist group Patriot Front marched through the Capitol Hill neighborhood as the nation marked its 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
Hundreds of masked members of the white supremacist organization Patriot Front marched through Washington, D.C. on July 4th, coinciding with the nation's 250th independence anniversary. The group gathered near Union Station before proceeding toward Capitol Hill, carrying banners including the Confederate flag.

The demonstrators wore white masks, khakis, and caps bearing the Patriot Front logo. Thomas Rousseau, the group's founder, appeared to lead the march through the capital as Independence Day festivities took place throughout the city.

cards.headline: Paul Pelosi involved in hit-and-run, may face misdemeanor charges
cards.teaser: The husband of former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi was involved in a hit-and-run in California that left a parked car with major damage.
cards.body:
Paul Pelosi, husband of former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, was involved in a hit-and-run incident in California that damaged a parked vehicle, authorities confirmed Saturday. The 86-year-old was driving his own vehicle at the time of the crash, which left the other car with major damage.

Pelosi may face misdemeanor charges related to the incident, according to the Napa County Sheriff's Office.

cards.headline: Five gubernatorial races emerge as most likely to flip parties
cards.teaser: Three dozen states are holding governor elections in November, with several battleground states testing the national political mood.
cards.body:
Thirty-six states are holding gubernatorial elections in November, with several races taking place in key battleground states that President Trump won in 2024. Swing states including Nevada, Georgia, and Wisconsin are drawing particular attention as indicators of the national political environment.

Two additional Midwestern states have also emerged as competitive races. These gubernatorial contests will test whether control of state offices shifts between parties in regions that historically influence broader political trends nationwide.

cards.headline: The Atlantic republishes JD Vance's 2016 essay critical of Trump
cards.teaser: The magazine republished Vice President Vance's essay from exactly 10 years ago, reviving critical comments he made about Trump before joining his administration.
cards.body:
The Atlantic republished Vice President Vance's essay, originally published exactly 10 years ago on July 4, 2016, bringing renewed attention to critical comments Vance made about President Trump before becoming his second vice president. The original article ran days after Vance published his bestselling memoir, Hillbilly Elegy.

The magazine included an editor's note with the republished piece. The essay contains some of the more pointed observations Vance made about Trump prior to his political transformation and eventual selection as vice president.
